note: Single source of truth for model choice (Claude and Codex tier tables; the Codex tier is used only when a second agent is enabled in config). Mirrored by claude/agents/*.md and codex/agents/*.toml, checked by modules/tools/scripts/tests. Human-readable policy: defaults/rules/ROUTING.md. Aliases, not pinned IDs, so a model retirement does not silently break routing. Project tier overrides: the config key routing.tier_overrides is the one path. DEPRECATED: a project's .ai/ROUTING.json (no code reads it; `sox project check` reports PRJ-ROUTING-LEGACY).
principles: Plan with the expensive tier once; execute with the cheaper tier; verify with a deterministic gate (tests, analyzers, finalizer) before trusting the result.
Send predictable, well-specified steps to the cheapest tier that passes the gate; escalate only the ambiguous remainder.
Escalate on evidence: a failed gate or a blocked report moves the task one tier up with the evidence attached, never repeated blind retries on the same tier.
Review and implementation use separate contexts; the reviewer is never the agent that wrote the change.

The session is a router: it plans, delegates to the tier agents, integrates and verifies; it works itself only on small things (one edit, one question, a few tool calls, or a brief longer than the work); no recursive delegation.
If the top tier or the high tier handles more than about 15 percent of tasks, routing is too conservative or tasks are harder than assumed: review the mix.

use: docs and tests from a spec

high.how: subagent with model opus or a separate session; the router stays on standard

top.rule: Only with owner approval: explain the reason, cost and expected gain first, then ask and wait for an explicit yes.

use: simple, fully specified, low-risk, easily verified work

top.rule: Never automatic. Analysis only, after multiple evidenced failed repairs, and only with owner approval after an explanation (attempts, evidence, scope). Approval does not authorize implementation, extra agents or xhigh effort.

escalation.queue: A standard run that reports blocked with escalate=true is retried once on high; a second failure goes to the owner.
escalation.interactive: After two failed attempts on a tier, stop, summarize evidence and move up one tier or ask the owner.
